gru_vs_lr_comparison.description: Compare GRU vs LogisticRegression on 16 session-level features (mean/std/max/slope)
gru_vs_lr_comparison.conclusion: LR matches GRU on F1, faster, interpretable, better cross-domain (0.4722 vs 0.25). Swap GRU -> LR recommended.

architecture_comparison.description: 5 architectures on 16 session-level features (mean/std/max/slope of 7 per-step features)

f1_diagnostic.description: Verify F1=1.0 is legitimate (not data leakage / eval bug)
f1_diagnostic.conclusion: F1=1.0 is legitimate — no data leakage, no eval bug, shuffle labels drop to 0.28. However, dataset is too easy: gap_mean alone gives F1=0.95, B2_score_mean gives 0.87. The real challenge is cross-domain generalization (A->B F1=0.47).

shuffle_test.description: Shuffle step order within each test session -> GRU should fail if learning sequence patterns
shuffle_test.conclusion: GRU does NOT learn sequence patterns. Shuffling changes nothing. RF on session averages (7 features) matches GRU performance (0.9965 vs 1.0). Branch 3 value is hybrid feature fusion, not sequence modeling.
shuffle_test.implication: Replace GRU with simpler classifier (RF/XGBoost). Reframe paper: session-level hybrid feature fusion, not sequence anomaly detection.
